summary: Iteration 109 RETEST of the 90-day document retention fix. All 6 backend tests pass. storage.delete_object() now correctly wipes object contents to 0 bytes via zero-byte PUT when Emergent Object Storage rejects DELETE (returned 'wiped'), retention.purge_expired_uploads() always tombstones the DB record with is_deleted=true / purged_at / purge_reason='retention_90d' / purge_outcome and $unset storage_path, a bogus-path old doc is still tombstoned without raising, recent docs are untouched, and a fresh upload + signed /api/files/{id} download still works right after a purge run. Purged file ids return 404 through /api/files/{id}, never 500. Log wording 'icerigi depodan silinemedi' + 'inceleyin' present in code. Retention scheduler boots ('document retention scheduler started' in backend log). Frontend homepage still renders data-testid='landing-ask-first' and data-testid='landing-commitments'.

action_items: OPTIONAL COPY REVIEW: Homepage promises 'Belgeleriniz 90 gün sonra otomatik siliniyor'. Technically the storage stub object remains in Emergent Object Storage (the platform still refuses HTTP DELETE with 405), we can only overwrite its bytes to zero. Content is destroyed and unreachable via /api/files (DB tombstone + no signed URL), so the customer-facing promise is honoured in spirit. If you want strict literal accuracy, consider softening the copy to 'içeriği 90 gün sonra imha ediliyor' or noting 'içerik geri getirilemeyecek şekilde 0 bayta indirilir'. Not blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: storage.delete_object() correctly handles both the 405 permanent-unsupported case (falls through the try/except without raising, then PUTs 0 bytes -> 'wiped') and network-level RequestException (logged as warning, still falls through to wipe). Good.

retention.py: DB tombstone now happens unconditionally in the loop body (not gated on storage success). Good. Consider surfacing purge_outcome='failed' distinctly if a future storage regression breaks the zero-byte PUT too - today a PUT failure would raise inside asyncio.to_thread and increment 'failed' but skip the tombstone (the tombstone update_one is after the outcome assignment). Minor: the except block sets outcome='failed' but does not continue, so the update_one still runs with outcome 'failed' - actually double-checked, the update DOES run, good; but note the 'failed' count is incremented AND the doc is still marked is_deleted=true which is the desired never-serve behaviour. Consistent with the spec.

storage.delete_object still does put_object even on generic exception from DELETE (only requests.RequestException is caught). If the DELETE call raises something else (e.g. connection reset wrapped differently), it will propagate. In practice requests wraps everything in RequestException so this is fine.
